newsitem.title: ITALY: Firm lira seen limiting Italy industry 1997 costs.
newsitem.headline: Firm lira seen limiting Italy industry 1997 costs.

text.p: The strength of the lira should hold down the cost of imported commodities for Italian manufacturers in the coming year, helping them to keep prices down and contain inflation, a study said on Wednesday.

The study by research group Prometeia and Fiat-Economic Studies said commodity prices were not expected to show signs of tension in the near future, and the appreciation of the lira would further limit their impact on Italian companies' costs.

It said the average lira price of 28 commodities was expected to rise by about one percent in 1997-98, so Italian industry could count on steel, copper and wood prices which were not significantly different from average prices paid in 1996.

"This will produce a situation which, if accompanied by an adequate dynamic of costs in other production areas, will allow Italian manufacturers to make another strong contribution to the process of falling inflation in Italy," the study said.

Italy's inflation rate in December was 2.6 percent year on year and after preliminary data from 11 sample cities published on Monday and Tuesday analysts forecast the consumer price index to remain at 2.6 percent in January.
